cards.text: Ezra the priest is facedown before the house of God, praying, confessing and weeping. And while he's down there, he's not alone for long.

cards.question: While Ezra prays facedown before the house of God, who gathers around him?

answers.text: A very large assembly of Israelites

cards.question: The crowd around Ezra is men, women and children, and they weep bitterly too.

cards.text: Then Shecaniah son of Jehiel, an Elamite, says it out loud to Ezra: we have been unfaithful to our God by marrying foreign women from the people of the land. Every meeting needs that ONE guy who finally says it out loud.

cards.question: Shecaniah admits Israel has been unfaithful, yet he says there is still ___ for Israel.

cards.text: And Shecaniah's got a plan. He wants it done according to the Law, following the counsel of those who tremble at the command of God.

cards.question: What covenant does Shecaniah want the people to make before God?

answers.text: Send away the foreign wives and their children
Rebuild the walls all around Jerusalem
Keep a fast for forty days and nights

cards.text: Then Shecaniah turns to Ezra: "Get up, for this matter is your responsibility" and he doesn't stop there.

cards.question: When Shecaniah tells Ezra to get up and take action, what does he promise him?

answers.text: The people will pick a new leader
The people will return to Babylon

cards.text: So Ezra gets up. I know that move, friend. I spent YEARS flat on my back in a junk drawer, and getting up is the hardest part.

cards.question: Ezra makes the leading priests, Levites and all Israel take an ___ to do what Shecaniah said.
The priests, Levites and all Israel refuse to take Ezra's oath.

cards.text: Then Ezra leaves the front of the house of God and walks to the chamber of a man named Jehohanan son of Eliashib. He's mourning over the unfaithfulness of the exiles.

cards.question: While Ezra stays in Jehohanan's chamber, he eats no food and drinks no water.

cards.text: Then a proclamation goes out across Judah and Jerusalem. Every exile, gather at Jerusalem.

cards.question: The exiles get ___ days to show up in Jerusalem.
What happens to any exile who doesn't show up in Jerusalem in time?

answers.text: He loses his property and is expelled from the assembly
He pays a fine in silver to the house of God
He is sent back to Babylon to live for good

cards.text: THREE DAYS. Not 'whenever you get a chance,' not 'let's circle back next week.' And within three days, all the men of Judah and Benjamin show up in Jerusalem.

cards.question: On the twentieth day of the ninth month, everyone sits in the square at the house of God, trembling over this matter. What else has them trembling?

cards.text: Picture it. Every man in Judah and Benjamin, sitting outside in the square in heavy rain. Friend, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer, and even I'm looking at that like, 'I'll stay in here, thanks.'
Then Ezra the priest stands up in front of all of them and says it plainly: "You have been unfaithful by marrying foreign women, adding to the guilt of Israel."

cards.question: Ezra tells them to make a confession to the LORD, do His will, and ___ themselves from the people of the land and from their foreign wives.
The whole assembly argues with Ezra and refuses to do what he says.

cards.text: They shout back, "Truly we must do as you say!" Then comes the BUT: there are a lot of people, it's the rainy season, they can't stay out in the open, and this isn't the work of one or two days.

cards.question: So what plan does the assembly suggest for handling it?

answers.text: Leaders represent everyone while towns come at set times
Everyone stays out in the square until it's all finished
Ezra settles every single case alone in one day

cards.question: In the assembly's plan, each town's men who married foreign women come at an appointed time with the ___ and ___ of their town.
Every single person in the assembly agrees with this plan.

cards.text: Only Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahzeiah son of Tikvah oppose the plan, with Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite supporting them.
But the exiles go ahead and do as proposed. Ezra the priest picks men to represent their families, every one of them identified by name.

cards.question: What kind of men does Ezra pick to represent their families?

cards.text: On the first day of the tenth month, they launch the investigation. Remember when the crowd said this wasn't the work of one or two days? They were NOT exaggerating.

cards.question: By the first day of the first month, they've dealt with all the men who married foreign women.

cards.text: Then comes the list, family by family, of every man who had married a foreign woman. It starts with priests from the family of Jeshua son of Jozadak, who pledged to send their wives away and gave a ram as a guilt offering. Then come Levites, a singer, gatekeepers and men from across Israel, and some of them had children by these wives.

findings.problem: The passage starts in the middle of Ezra's prayer, which continues from Ezra 9. The opening card never says what Ezra is confessing (the people's unfaithfulness in marrying foreign women) or who he is praying to. The baker gets 'praying, confessing and weeping' with no context for the confession.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The joke 'Every meeting needs that ONE guy who finally says it out loud' suggests nobody had said it before Shecaniah. The text shows Ezra was making this very confession aloud before the house of God (Ezra 10:1). The card also repeats 'says it out loud' twice, which weakens the punchline.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'inventory' seems chosen only to fit 'an' before a vowel. 'Take an inventory to do what Shecaniah said' makes no sense, so it isn't the same kind of thing as 'oath' and 'offering' and reads as silly.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: This story card adds nothing new from the passage. It restates Ezra 10:9 (the men sitting in the square in heavy rain), which cards 18 and 19 already covered, and then adds a joke. It is a recap card. Its joke also reuses the 'I spent YEARS in a junk drawer' opener from card 10 in the same stop.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: The question 'So what plan does the assembly suggest for handling it?' points back with 'it' to a card the baker can no longer see. It never says what is being handled: dealing with the men who married foreign women.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Story card 4 says they can't stay out in the open and that this isn't the work of one or two days. That rules out both wrong answers: 'Everyone stays out in the square until it's all finished' and 'Ezra settles every single case alone in one day'. The right answer is the only one left.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The two-blank question 'with the ___ and ___ of their town' assigns 'elders' to blank 1 and 'judges' to blank 2. A baker who puts 'judges and elders' has the same meaning but would be marked wrong, because the order is only fixed by the BSB wording.
findings.question: For a two-blank fill in the blank where the two right words could swap places without changing the meaning, should either order count as right, or should the card be rewritten so only one order makes sense?
